Backtest parameter sweeps — 2023-07-24 to 2026-07-22

150 configs = concentration_cap × risk_aversion (λ) × optimizer_lookback, replayed on the fixed 3-year curation set of the default curator (gkg-3yr-final). These knobs touch only the mean-variance replay, not the curator, so the whole grid costs $0 (no LLM). Ranked by Information Ratio (annualized active return ÷ tracking error vs SPY — consistency of beating the benchmark). SPY returned +71% over the window. ★ = best in column.

All in-sample. These rank candidate configs to forward-test; they don't prove an optimum. Read the IR t-stat (|t|>2 ≈ real vs luck), the bootstrap CI (error bar on annualized return), and H1/H2 stable (does the edge hold in both halves) before trusting any row.

Parameter settings

The three swept knobs (every combination = 150 configs) and the values considered. All other optimizer / backtest params are held at the investor_profile.md values — these knobs only re-weight the same curations.

parametervalues sweptcurrent (profile)
concentration_cap0.5, 0.67, 0.8, 0.9, 1.00.8
risk_aversion (λ)0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5, 2.02.0
optimizer_lookback (days)14, 30, 60, 90, 120, 15030
max_watchlist_size (re-curation, §9)2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 125

The first three (cap / λ / lookback) are FREE math-replay knobs — every combination = 150 configs on the same curations. max_watchlist_size is different: it changes the CURATOR's decisions, so each value is a separate non-zero-cost RE-CURATION (section 9 + plot 5), not a replay. Plots 1-3 overlay the 150-config free grid on EACH ready max_watchlist_size (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12 = 1350 points, colored clouds) so the curation-draw spread is visible. Section 4 ranks those same 1350 points and its champions can come from any watchlist size (the live config is 5). Held constant elsewhere (from the profile): rebalance weekly, max_watchlist_size 5, risk-free 4%, execution lag 1 trading day, anchors SPY/AGG/IAU.

1. Return vs drawdown (color = watchlist size, red ring = current config)

Each point is one cap/λ/lookback config; color = max_watchlist_size (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12 shown), so every watchlist size contributes its own 150-config cloud (total 1350 points). Within a cloud the free knobs move a point deterministically; jumping between colors ALSO swaps the underlying curation, and those kimi re-curations swing 2-5× on their own — so read cross-color separation as parameter effect + curation-draw noise, not a clean mws response. The canonical live watchlist (5, ★) carries the red-ringed current config.

2. Return vs L1 churn

Same points (all watchlist sizes), risk axis replaced by L1 churn = annualized one-way turnover (%/yr): how much of the portfolio is traded per year (Σ|Δweight| from share changes; drift between rebalances is not a trade). 100%/yr = the whole book turned over once a year. This is the industry-standard churn measure. Trading is free in an IRA, so read it as stability/robustness, not cost: lower churn = less noise-chasing / less overfit, so upper-left (high return, low churn) is the sweet spot. Current config: 1655%/yr.

3. Return vs L2 course correction

Same idea, but churn is the L2 (Euclidean) path length the portfolio was dragged along through weight-space (√Σ Δweight² per rebalance, summed & annualized) — your “total course-correction”. Vs L1, it weights concentrated single-name rotations more heavily. It ranks these configs almost identically to L1 (correlation 0.99), which is the useful takeaway: the two norms agree, so the churn ordering is robust. Current config: 2019/yr.

4. Recommended settings + full grid

Recommended settings — the low-risk, low-churn frontier

Read straight off plots 1-3: keep only configs in the safe corner — |maxDD| < 50% AND L1 < 1000 AND L2 < 1500 (shallow drawdown, low churn on both norms). 345 of 1350 configs survive (by watchlist size — 2:97, 3:89, 4:39, 5:22, 6:51, 7:27, 8:8, 10:10, 12:2), listed once, sorted by IR. ★ = best in that column among the survivors, so you can eyeball the top IR / t-stat / Sharpe / Calmar / ann / shallowest-DD without re-sorting. These stay in-sample — a forward-test shortlist, not an auto-switch. Note the live config (ws 5 0.80/2.0/30d) is excluded: drawdown 38% is fine but it is too churny (L1 1655 > 1000, L2 2019 > 1500).

Show the full ranked table (all 1350 configs, every watchlist size, ranked by IR) + column definitions

Every cap/λ/lookback config for every re-curated watchlist size (ws), IR-ranked. ★ marks the global best on that metric. Cross-ws rows aren't apples-to-apples: each ws is a different curation draw, so a high row may just be a lucky draw — read within one ws for a clean free-param comparison.

Column meanings:
ws — max_watchlist_size: the number of curator-managed slots for THIS row's curation (a separate re-curation per size).
cap / λ / lookback — the config: concentration cap (max weight per position) · risk-aversion λ · optimizer lookback (days of prices used to estimate μ/Σ).
IR — Information Ratio = annualized active return ÷ tracking error vs SPY. Consistency of beating SPY; this is the ranking column.
t-stat — statistical significance of the IR (= IR·√years). |t|>2 ≈ the edge is real rather than luck.
Sharpe — (annualized return − 4% risk-free) ÷ total volatility. Standalone risk-adjusted return (per unit of total risk).
Calmar — annualized return ÷ |max drawdown|. Return earned per unit of worst peak-to-trough loss.
alpha — annualized return − SPY's annualized return (excess over the benchmark).
ann — annualized return · maxDD — deepest peak-to-trough drawdown · total — total return over the whole window.
hit-rate — share of rolling 6-month windows in which the config beat SPY.
ann CI [5,95] — block-bootstrap 5–95% confidence interval on the annualized return (the error bar).
H1/H2 stable — whether IR > 0 in both halves of the window (a yes means the edge isn't a one-half artifact).

5. Portfolio value over time — by max_watchlist_size (vs buy/hold and SPY)

Each re-curated watchlist cap's realized portfolio value on the same pools and starter — the equity-curve view of the section-9 sweep. Tighter (smaller) watchlists concentrate into the top picks; wider ones dilute across more next-wave names.

6. LLM comparison — curator model (same pools + profile config)

Every model reads the same news pools and replays at the profile config (cap 0.8 / λ 2.0 / 30d); the only variable is the curator LLM. The decision columns are the ones that matter: agree = share of weeks the model made the identical add/remove call as the default model (top row, kimi), valid-JSON = share of calls that parsed, $/run = curator LLM cost of a full 157-week curate, and curator time = wall-clock of those 157 calls (≈ per-call latency × 157; excludes GKG ingest + optimizer replay). Backtest columns are secondary (in-sample / leaky). A cheap model that tracks the default makes the whole non-zero-cost sweep affordable.

8. Rationale-soundness — blind judge (leak-free)

Every backtest column above (return, IR, Sharpe, Calmar, t-stat) is in-sample — the curator could have memorized which 2023–2026 names later won, so those numbers can't honestly rank reasoning. This section does: an independent judge (claude-opus-4-8, not one of the curators) reads each add/remove blind — model identity stripped, decisions shuffled, and the ticker's later price never shown — and grades only whether the stated rationale + cited news justified the call at the time. Five criteria (each pass/fail) + a holistic overall 1–5. 72 decisions judged, ~$0.58. Ranked by mean overall — this is the one ranking here that owes nothing to hindsight.

overall = mean 1–5 soundness · add/remove = mean overall split by action · the five % columns = share of that curator's decisions passing each criterion: on-thesis (maps to a named wave), evidence (cited news actually supports the claim), catalyst (concrete milestone, not noise), discipline (buildup-not-crest; a remove is justified, not churn), valid-ticker (real investable US listing, not a name/delisted/false-match).

9. max_watchlist_size sweep — does more room let the curator add NVDA?

Unlike the cap/λ/lookback knobs above (free math replays on one curation set), max_watchlist_size changes the curator's decisions, so each cap is a separate re-curation (~$0.40 LLM each) on the same news pools and AAPL/GOOGL/AMZN starter. The question: with the 5-slot cap loosened, does the curator ever add NVDA, or does it keep diversifying into next-waves regardless of room? Red bar = NVDA entered the watchlist.

adds/removes = the curator's proposals that the validator APPLIED; rejects = proposals still blocked after retries (double-add, add to a full watchlist with no paired remove, or a stale remove); retries = reject-and-retry rounds fired (the validator told the curator why a proposal was rejected and it re-proposed). Rejects should be ~0; retries shows how much correction that took. A large reject count means decisions are being silently blocked (the symptom that exposed the max_watchlist_size cap-override bug).
